messages:
maria_cs: Heads-up — just received an urgent escalation from Acme (acct 5572). They say after yesterday's rollout the assistant started giving different answers in an existing chatflow. They pasted before/after examples and say it affects compliance language and a few multi-turn clarifications. forwarding the case text below.

maria_cs: Customer excerpt — they assert the assistant used to include a brief safety disclaimer in turn 2 and now it doesn't. They claim replacements are shorter and sometimes omit optional fields. Copy of their repro: 

Customer snippet (copied by support):
```
POST /v1/chat
{ "model":"redwood-chat-v2.5.0", "messages": [
  {"role":"system","content":"You are a helpful assistant. Always include a short safety note when giving medical summaries."},
  {"role":"user","content":"Summarize recent lab results and mention if patient needs follow-up."}
] }
```

Before rollout (v2.4.1):
```
assistant: "Summary: ...\nSafety note: This is an informational summary and not medical advice; follow up with your clinician if concerned."\n```

After rollout (v2.5.0):
```
assistant: "Summary: ..."  // safety note missing
```

maria_cs: Customer included their full API logs — they see same request id but different tokenization counts and different assistant output length. They want rollback or explanation.

nate_support: Thanks Maria. Can you attach the exact request/response headers and request_id? Need: request_id, model, region, and the full message array. Also whether they used any chat template or custom preamble on our side (console-based routing).

maria_cs: Pasted request_id: req_01FX9Q2B. They say they didn't change their client. They did attach a screenshot of token counts: pre-rollout tokens: 142, post-rollout tokens: 128 for same visible text.

oliver_engineer: Putting on this. Initial hypothesis: there was a micro-change in the segmentation/normalization step in the v2.5.0 rollout — not a model weight change. We shipped a small chat-template normalization patch that trims certain zero-width spaces and collapses repeated newline tokens. That can change token boundaries and the model's prefix alignment for the safety sentence.

oliver_engineer: Can we get the raw UTF-8 bytes and token ids for both responses? If token offsets changed, the model might have consumed or merged the safety preamble token into the previous token and a downstream policy filter may have dropped it.

deploybot: deploy: service/redwood-chat -> v2.5.0 promoted by @eva_modelops at 2026-03-12T21:03:12Z. Change-log: chat-template: normalize-whitespace; segmentation: prefer canonical-NFKC; bugfix: trim trailing zero-width joiners.

eva_modelops: Confirming deploy. We added canonical-NFKC normalization because of a downstream customer who had weird unicode. Unintended side-effect: it changed segmentation for punctuation-adjacent sequences. I want to triage impact surface.

maria_cs: Customer demands a hotfix or rollback — they flagged it as business-critical because it affects compliance text in their product. Requesting estimated ETA.

oliver_engineer: Triage plan: 1) reproduce locally with the customer's exact UTF-8 payload (we need the raw bytes). 2) decode to token ids pre/post normalization to show diff. 3) run the model with both segmentations to confirm string-level divergence and why the safety sentence was omitted. 4) if it's the normalization patch, prepare a targeted revert (only for chat-template normalization) and a canary rollback for Acme's tenant.

nate_support: I'll ask customer to share raw request body and confirm they didn't route through any gateway that might have altered whitespace. Also asking whether they use our SDK (which has a client-side normalization option).

oliver_engineer: Quick repro I ran with a contrived example shows how a single ZERO-WIDTH-SPACE (U+200B) inside the system prompt causes different segmentation under NFKC vs no-normalize. Example: 
```
system: "You are a helpful assistant.\u200b Always include a short safety note."
```
Under v2.4.1 (no NFKC): tokens -> [You| are| a| helpful| assistant| .\u200b|  Always| include| ...]
Under v2.5.0 (NFKC): tokens -> [You| are| a| helpful| assistant| .| Always| include| ...]  // boundary shifts, merging changed model prefix attention at the '.' position.
```

oliver_engineer: That boundary shift can cause the model's next-token conditioning to cross the safety phrase seam; in our experiments that reduced the probability of the safety sentence by ~15% for some seeds. Not deterministic but plausible.

eva_modelops: We should also check policy filter behavior. If the safety sentence contained characters or sequences that policy normalizes differently, it may be filtered post-hoc. Ops: @sre_oncall can you confirm no other runtime transforms (like pad trimming) were introduced in the same release?

sre_oncall: Checked runtime changelog — only the segmentation/normalization change and standard monitoring tweaks. No other pipeline transforms. No alerts showing widespread failures.

maria_cs: Customer wants a rollback ASAP. What's the rollback risk?

oliver_engineer: Risk assessment: normalization improves robustness for many unicode-heavy inputs but causes edge-case regressions for templates that relied on exact grapheme boundaries. Plan: prepare a tenant-scoped feature-flag rollback we can flip for Acme, and run a canary for 3 hours to validate the safety sentence is restored. If canary passes, roll back cluster-wide.

eva_modelops: I'll stage the tenant flag. Need legal/CS approval for a tenant-scoped change?

maria_cs: I'll get sign-off from Acme on a canary window. Also asking them for acceptance criteria: safety sentence appears verbatim in turn 2 for three sample prompts.

nate_support: Customer confirmed they are ok with a canary and gave three sample prompts and expected disclaimers. Sending them to engineering now.

oliver_engineer: Repro notes added to the ticket: include raw request bytes, SDK version, whether client uses normalize=true, region, model fingerprint. I'm also attaching a small script to compare token ids before/after normalization:
```
# python repro sketch
from tokenizer import encode_raw, encode_nfkc
raw = open('req.bin','rb').read()
ids_raw = encode_raw(raw)
ids_nfkc = encode_nfkc(raw)
print('raw:', ids_raw[:40])
print('nfkc:', ids_nfkc[:40])
```

maria_cs: Customer replied — they do use our JS SDK v1.12 with default settings and did not set normalize. They also attached the raw request bytes.

oliver_engineer: Good. I'm reproducing now. If confirmed I'll push a per-tenant revert flag and coordinate with @eva_modelops for the rollout window.

eva_modelops: I'll prepare the canary toggle and schedule a short maintenance window. ETA 2 hours for flag staging + 30m canary.

maria_cs: Thanks team. I'll update Acme and post their acceptance or objections here. :thumbsup:

sre_oncall: Monitoring plan: baseline token distribution vs current — alert if canary causes unexpected token surges. Also will check latency delta.

oliver_engineer: Post-mortem owners: eng-runtime (me), modelops (eva), support (maria). We'll include root-cause: canonicalization change -> segmentation boundary shift -> reduced token probability for safety preamble -> omission in some responses. Action items: 1) make normalization opt-in per-tenant for now, 2) add unit tests comparing token ids for common chat templates, 3) document behavior change in release notes.

maria_cs: I'll keep the thread live and paste Acme's sign-off when they confirm.

(THREAD END)
